meta.title: Nadia's Gecko File
meta.textType: functional: an animal fact file in an email, with a diagram

paragraphs: On Monday, January twenty-fifth, Mia opened an email from her pen pal Nadia. The subject was "My gecko file." Lily stood beside the desk and looked at the screen. Nadia wrote, "Dear Mia, here is my fact file about geckos." It had a photo of a pale gecko on a wall and three headings. The first heading was "Where geckos live." "Wild geckos live in warm places, on walls, on ceilings, and in trees," Nadia wrote. "Some types are about ten centimeters in length." The second heading was "What geckos eat." "They come out at night, and they eat insects." "Few people see them in the day." "They are good friends of a house, because they eat the small insects that we do not like."

The third heading was "How geckos climb." Under it there was a small diagram. It showed the toe of a gecko with a pale, soft pad and tiny hairs. Arrows pointed to the words "toe," "pad," "tiny hairs," and "wall." "A gecko has several toes, and each toe has a pad with many tiny hairs," Nadia wrote. "The hairs hold the wall, so the gecko does not fall." "That is how a gecko walks on a ceiling." "The hairs are very small, but they are strong," said Lily.

Mia took her notebook and drew a small gecko on a ceiling. Under the drawing, she wrote, "Nadia: geckos eat insects at night." Then Lily pointed at the wall above the desk. A small pale gecko sat there, and it did not move. "Look, we have a visitor," she whispered. Pip came into the room and sat on the floor. He looked up at the gecko. He gave a small bark. The gecko was fast. It ran to a small hole near the window.

Mia read the last lines of the email. "Do you have geckos at home?" Nadia asked. "Does Pip like them?" "Is it true that geckos are lucky for a house?" "Best wishes, Nadia." "Pip does not like them, but they are lucky for a house," said Mia. "A gecko is not as big as Pip's red ball," said Lily. "But it is much faster than he is."

The girls wrote an answer to Nadia. "Dear Nadia, thank you for the fact file." "We have a small gecko in Mia's room." "It is not as long as a pencil." "Best wishes, Mia and Lily." Mia clicked send. The two girls smiled, because the small creature was safe in its hole.
text.summary: Mia reads an email from her pen pal Nadia with a fact file about geckos. The file tells where geckos live, what they eat, and how they climb, and then the girls find a small gecko on the wall.
